**← Back to [EAP Home](../../README.md) • [Resources](../README.md)**

### 1.1 Competency Areas

<!-- synthesia-video-url: https://share.synthesia.io/638a32d1-f1f6-4eba-b219-7fd6df62b999 | ../../assets/images/synthesia/training-thumbnail.png -->

The EA practice defines core and cross-cutting competency areas that form the foundation of architectural excellence:
page_texts.5:
[resources/training/README.md#111-core-architecture-domains]

#### 1.1.1 Core Architecture Domains

**Business Architecture**

- **Business Process Modeling**: Understanding and documenting business processes and workflows
- **Capability Mapping**: Identifying and mapping business capabilities to technology solutions
- **Requirements Analysis**: Gathering, analyzing, and translating business requirements
- **Stakeholder Management**: Effective communication and collaboration with business stakeholders
- **Value Stream Mapping**: Understanding end-to-end value delivery processes

**Application Architecture**

- **Application Design**: Creating comprehensive application architectures that meet business needs
- **Application Portfolio Management**: Managing the enterprise application landscape
- **Integration Patterns**: Designing effective integration strategies and patterns
- **Service Design**: Architecting microservices and service-oriented solutions
- **API Standards**: Establishing and implementing API design standards

**Information Architecture**

- **Data Modeling**: Designing effective data models and structures
- **Data Governance**: Implementing data governance frameworks and policies
- **Analytics Architecture**: Designing data analytics and reporting solutions
- **Data Quality Management**: Ensuring data quality and integrity
- **Information Flows**: Designing effective data integration and information exchange patterns

**Infrastructure Architecture**

- **Cloud Architecture**: Designing cloud-native and hybrid infrastructure solutions
- **Infrastructure Patterns**: Establishing reusable infrastructure patterns and templates
- **Deployment Models**: Designing deployment architectures and strategies
- **Platform Standards**: Defining and implementing platform standards

**Technology Architecture**

- **Technology Standards**: Establishing technology selection criteria and standards
- **Platform Services**: Architecting platform service offerings
- **Integration Platforms**: Designing integration middleware and platforms
- **Development Tools**: Selecting and standardizing development tooling

**ITSM & Operations Architecture**

- **DevSecOps Practices**: Implementing DevSecOps and platform engineering practices
- **Monitoring & Observability**: Designing monitoring and observability solutions
- **Incident Management**: Architecting operational support systems
- **Performance Optimization**: Ensuring solutions meet performance requirements
page_texts.6:
[resources/training/README.md#112-cross-cutting-architecture-domains]

#### 1.1.2 Cross-Cutting Architecture Domains

**Security Architecture**

- **Security Framework Design**: Creating comprehensive security architectures
- **Threat Modeling**: Identifying and analyzing potential security threats
- **Compliance Requirements**: Understanding and implementing regulatory compliance
- **Risk Management**: Assessing and managing security risks
- **Zero-Trust Architecture**: Implementing modern security paradigms

**Governance Architecture**

- **Architecture Governance**: Implementing architecture review and governance processes
- **Policy Management**: Establishing and enforcing architectural policies
- **Standards Enforcement**: Ensuring compliance with architectural standards
- **Quality Assurance**: Implementing quality gates and architectural reviews
- **Decision Management**: Facilitating and documenting architectural decisions

**AI/ML Architecture**

- **AI Integration Patterns**: Designing architectures that incorporate AI/ML capabilities
- **MLOps**: Implementing machine learning operations and lifecycle management
- **AI-Enhanced Software Engineering**: Leveraging AI to improve development practices
- **Strategic AI Integration**: Incorporating AI into business capabilities
- **Intelligent System Design**: Architecting systems that leverage artificial intelligence
- **LLM Integration**: Implementing Large Language Model solutions and architectures
- **RAG Architectures**: Designing Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems for enhanced AI responses
page_texts.7:
[resources/training/README.md#113-healthcare-technology-architecture]

#### 1.1.3 Healthcare Technology Architecture

- **X12 EDI Standards**: Understanding and implementing Medicaid transaction standards for claims processing (837, 835, 834, 270/271, 276/277, 278)
- **NCPDP Standards**: Understanding pharmacy transaction standards (D.0, SCRIPT, Telecommunication, Batch)
- **FHIR/HL7 Standards**: Understanding healthcare interoperability standards for data exchange
- **HIPAA Compliance**: Ensuring privacy and security compliance in healthcare
- **Healthcare Analytics**: Designing population health and Medicaid program analytics solutions
- **Medicaid Workflows**: Understanding Medicaid-specific administrative and operational workflows
page_texts.9:
[resources/training/README.md#121-foundational-level-0-2-years]

#### 1.2.1 Foundational Level (0-2 years)

**Learning Objectives:**

- Understand basic architectural concepts and principles
- Develop domain-specific knowledge in primary area of focus
- Learn fundamental technology platforms and tools
- Build basic business analysis and communication skills

**Core Curriculum:**

- Enterprise Architecture Fundamentals
- Domain-Specific Basics (choice of Business, Application, Information, Infrastructure, Technology, ITSM/Operations, Security, Governance, AI/ML, or Healthcare)
- AWS Cloud Platform Basics
- Business Analysis Fundamentals
- Communication and Documentation Skills

**Suggested Topics:**

- Skills assessment and knowledge validation
- Project-based learning with mentorship
- Portfolio development of architectural artifacts
page_texts.10:
[resources/training/README.md#122-intermediate-level-2-5-years]

#### 1.2.2 Intermediate Level (2-5 years)

**Learning Objectives:**

- Develop advanced design and problem-solving capabilities
- Master stakeholder management and communication
- Demonstrate technical leadership on projects
- Contribute to architectural standards and best practices

**Suggested Topics:**

- Advanced Architecture Design Patterns
- Stakeholder Management and Communication
- Technical Leadership Skills
- Advanced Domain Specialization
- Cross-Domain Integration

**Assessment Approaches:**

- Stakeholder feedback
- Project outcome evaluation and business impact
- Peer recognition and collaboration effectiveness
- Contribution to architectural standards and patterns
page_texts.11:
[resources/training/README.md#123-advanced-level-5-years]

#### 1.2.3 Advanced Level (5+ years)

**Learning Objectives:**

- Develop strategic thinking and enterprise-wide perspective
- Master innovation and emerging technology evaluation
- Demonstrate organizational leadership and mentoring
- Drive architectural vision and transformation

**Suggested Topics:**

- Strategic Architecture Planning
- Innovation and Emerging Technology Evaluation
- Organizational Leadership and Change Management
- Advanced Mentoring and Coaching Skills
- Industry Thought Leadership

**Assessment Approaches:**

- Business impact and strategic contribution measurement
- Innovation contributions and technology adoption
- Leadership effectiveness and team development
- Industry recognition and thought leadership

##### Junior Architect → Senior Architect → Principal Architect → Senior Principal Architect

| Level                            | Experience | Key Responsibilities                               | Competency Requirements                           |
| -------------------------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| **Junior Architect**             | 0-3 years  | Component design, documentation support            | Foundational competencies                         |
| **Senior Architect**             | 3-7 years  | Solution design, stakeholder interaction           | Intermediate competencies + specialization        |
| **Principal Architect**          | 7-12 years | Complex solution leadership, standards development | Advanced competencies + cross-domain expertise    |
| **Senior Principal Architect**   | 12+ years  | Technology vision, industry thought leadership     | Expert-level competencies + innovation leadership |
page_texts.31:
[resources/training/README.md#team-lead--architecture-manager--director-of-architecture--vp-architecture]

##### Team Lead → Architecture Manager → Director of Architecture → VP Architecture

| Level                    | Experience  | Key Responsibilities                                          | Requirements                                                |
| ------------------------ | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Team Lead**            | 5-8 years   | Small team management, project coordination                   | Senior architect competencies + leadership skills              |
| **Architecture Manager** | 8-12 years  | Department management, strategy development                   | Principal architect competencies + management experience       |
| **Director**             | 12-18 years | Multi-department oversight, executive interaction             | Senior principal architect competencies + strategic leadership |
| **VP Architecture**      | 18+ years   | Enterprise architecture vision, organizational transformation | Expert competencies + executive leadership                     |

[resources/training/README.md#322-performance-rating-scale]

#### 3.2.2 Performance Rating Scale

| Rating                    | Description                       | Performance Indicators                                                         |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Exceptional (5)**       | Consistently exceeds expectations | Industry recognition, significant business impact, innovation leadership       |
| **Exceeds (4)**           | Regularly surpasses goals         | Strong stakeholder feedback, successful complex projects, mentoring excellence |
| **Meets (3)**             | Satisfies all requirements        | Competent technical delivery, good collaboration, steady improvement           |
| **Developing (2)**        | Working toward expectations       | Some gaps in delivery, needs additional support, showing improvement           |
| **Needs Improvement (1)** | Below expectations                | Significant performance gaps, requires performance improvement plan            |

[resources/training/README.md#80-conclusion]

## 8.0 Conclusion

The Training & Development Framework provides a foundation for building architectural capabilities at Gainwell that align with our focus on Medicaid payer systems. This framework emphasizes practical, topic-oriented learning rather than prescriptive programs, allowing flexibility as we develop our training approach.

**Key Focus Areas:**

- Core competency development across business, application, information, infrastructure, technology, ITSM/operations, security, governance, and AI/ML architecture domains
- Medicaid-specific healthcare architecture expertise including X12 EDI, NCPDP, FHIR/HL7, and HIPAA compliance
- AWS cloud platform knowledge and skills
- Career progression pathways supporting both individual contributor and management tracks
- Knowledge sharing and collaboration through mentorship and peer learning

This framework will evolve as our Enterprise Architecture practice matures. The emphasis is on building foundational elements first, then expanding capabilities over time based on organizational needs and priorities.

Success depends on active participation, leadership support, and our collective commitment to continuous learning and architectural excellence in service of Medicaid beneficiaries and state partners.
